sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Hamilton Township, Atlantic County, NJ?
sections.html:
Owners here can list, sell privately or take a cash offer, and the pace of any of them depends on a few local steps: a resale inspection through the township, a tax payoff and a deed recorded at the courthouse in Mays Landing. This page covers Hamilton Township in Atlantic County, not the Hamilton near Trenton in Mercer County.

The Census Bureau estimates 28,845 residents for July 1, 2025, up 5.0 percent from the 2020 base. About 70.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the median value is $246,200, and listings range from suburban streets in the developed east to rural lots in the pine forest of the west.

sections.h2: What makes Hamilton Township different from other Atlantic County towns?
sections.html:
Hamilton Township has the largest land area of any municipality in New Jersey at 110.90 square miles, and the township calls itself New Jersey's largest municipality. Only Galloway Township is bigger when water is counted. Mays Landing, the Atlantic County seat since the county formed in 1837, lies inside the township, along with the census-designated places of McKee City and Mizpah.

Much of that land is protected. The township is part of the New Jersey Pinelands National Reserve, and the Pinelands Commission regulates development across the western three-quarters, which stays pine forest and rural. The eastern quarter is a Regional Growth Area where development is allowed and encouraged, and most residents live there, near the Hamilton Mall and other retail centers.

  • Mays Landing: 5,603 residents in 2020 and the site of the county courthouse complex.
  • McKee City: 9,758 residents in 2020, the largest census-designated place in the township.
  • Lake Lenape and the Great Egg Harbor River: recreation areas, with the Lake Lenape parks covering more than 2,000 acres.

If the house sits on or near undeveloped land, ask the township's planning and zoning office whether the parcel falls inside the Pinelands Area before you describe what a buyer can add or build.

sections.h2: How did Hamilton Township grow into the place it is now?
sections.html:
Hamilton Township was incorporated on February 5, 1813, from parts of Egg Harbor and Weymouth townships. Its early economy followed the Great Egg Harbor River: a shipyard and trading post opened near Babcock Creek at Mays Landing in 1756, and more than 200 vessels were built along the river between 1830 and 1880.

The population stood at 6,017 in 1960, 16,012 in 1990 and 27,484 in 2020. Retail is part of the local economy, with more than 3,000,000 square feet of stores including Hamilton Mall, Consumer Square and Hamilton Commons, and a winery on a 57-acre vineyard.

sections.h2: What inspection does Hamilton Township require before I sell?
sections.html:
The township's fire inspectors check smoke and carbon monoxide detectors before a house is resold or reoccupied, and the request goes through the township's online title transfer inspection portal, linked from the Fire Prevention page. State rules require a smoke alarm certificate before a one-family or two-family house is sold, leased or reoccupied, and the municipality is the only source of that certificate.

Construction office inspections can be scheduled in person at the township hall at 6101 Thirteenth Street in Mays Landing or by fax, and the office says it does not take inspection requests by phone. A certificate lasts six months, so ask for the inspection when you have an accepted contract and a closing date, not months ahead.

  • Working smoke alarms on each floor, including the basement, and near sleeping areas.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm where the code calls for one.
  • Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms when you replace old units.

The Code Enforcement Bureau also enforces the property maintenance code on complaints, so clear any open code issues before you list.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and appeals work in Hamilton Township?
sections.html:
Assessment appeals go to the Atlantic County Board of Taxation at 5909 Main Street in Mays Landing. Petitions must reach the board by 4:00 p.m. on April 1, a postmark does not count, and added or omitted assessment petitions are due by 4:00 p.m. on December 1. The 2026 April filing deadline has passed.

Filing is available online at MyNJAppeal.com, where you can upload evidence up to seven days before your hearing. Assessment notices usually arrive in late January, and the board points owners to its lists of usable comparable sales. The question to ask is whether the assessment is more than you could sell the house for.

Ask the township tax collector for a payoff figure before closing, and look up the parcel on the county's property assessment search before you set a price.

sections.h2: What closing costs and recording steps apply in Hamilton Township?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee at recording, and on a price at or below $350,000 the state charges $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 per $500 to $200,000 and $3.90 per $500 above that, so a $325,000 sale carries a $1,910 fee. The township's average 2025 sale of about $312,000 falls in that lower bracket.

The deed is recorded at the Atlantic County Clerk's main office, the Historic Court House Complex at 5901 Main Street in Mays Landing, which is inside the township. A satellite office operates at 1333 Atlantic Avenue in Atlantic City. Checks for recording and transfer fees are payable to the Atlantic County Clerk's Office, and any Gross Income Tax payment for a nonresident seller goes to the State of New Jersey Division of Taxation.

  • Seller's residency certification (GIT/REP-3) for New Jersey residents.
  • Estimated Gross Income Tax payment, minimum 2 percent of the price, for nonresident sellers.
  • Deed prepared by the closing attorney or title company.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and transit serve Hamilton Township buyers?
sections.html:
Hamilton Township Schools serve prekindergarten through eighth grade in three schools: Shaner Memorial, the George Hess Educational Complex and William Davies Middle School. Ninth through twelfth graders attend Oakcrest High School in the township, part of the Greater Egg Harbor Regional High School District. Atlantic Cape Community College's Mays Landing campus has operated since 1968.

A 14-mile stretch of the Atlantic City Expressway runs through the township with three interchanges, and U.S. Routes 40 and 322 and Route 50 add east-west and north-south options. NJ Transit bus routes 502 and 553 reach Atlantic City, and the 315 runs between Cape May and Philadelphia.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell a house in Hamilton Township, Atlantic County?
faqs.a: Yes, the township's fire inspectors check smoke and carbon monoxide detectors before resale, and the request goes through the online title transfer inspection portal. New Jersey law requires the certificate for one-family and two-family houses.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for a Hamilton Township sale?
faqs.a: At the Atlantic County Clerk's Office, 5901 Main Street in Mays Landing, which is within the township. A satellite office is at 1333 Atlantic Avenue in Atlantic City.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Hamilton Township?
faqs.a: April 1 at 4:00 p.m., with a December 1 deadline for added or omitted assessments. Filing is available online, and a postmark does not meet the deadline.

faqs.q: Is Hamilton Township in Atlantic County the same as Hamilton in Mercer County?
faqs.a: No, they are separate municipalities in different counties with different tax boards, clerks and inspection offices. This page is about the one around Mays Landing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hamilton Township house inside the Pinelands?
faqs.a: Yes. Pinelands rules govern what can be built, so ask the township planning and zoning office what the parcel's zone allows before you advertise additions or lot splits.
